comment: Groups that may skip cases in CI, with the reason, an owner, the one `case` the entry excuses and an `expires` date (scripts/ci.py check-skips; docs/building.md, 'Skips'). A group that is not here must run in CI: if it skips wholesale the run fails. Every entry names exactly one case (there is no whole-group entry) and expires on its date: an expired entry is an error until it is renewed with a new reason. The reason matches the start of the skip's reason (a skip usually carries detail after the entry's words); the case matches exactly. A skip whose reason names a tool the dev shell (flake.nix, devShells.default) must provide is a failure even for a group here. Prefer fixing the shell or the test to adding an entry.

groups.case: Verilog: Icarus Verilog accepts the emitted modules (skipped without iverilog on PATH)
groups.why: Icarus simulation is optional in the dev shell; yosys (synthesis) is required and is in flake.nix, so a 'no yosys' skip in this group still fails.

groups.case: from source: install, channels, update, shims, +SPEC, run
groups.why: the 'from source' case needs Lake's toolchain inside a checkout, which the store-built shards do not have; the rest of the group runs.

groups.case: prelude surface: `import Prelude` alone carries `IO` in the self-hosted toolchain only
groups.reason: prelude: the self-hosted Prelude is one embedded module that includes the IO natives
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (A14/C12): the self-hosted Prelude embeds the IO natives; the host's lib/Prelude.wiz has none. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: --target llvm|wasm: the host selects the backend, the self-hosted one emits C only (C5)
groups.reason: backend: --target llvm/wasm selects LLVM/WebAssembly in the host (C5)
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (C5): the self-hosted backend emits C only and refuses the other target names. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: build: a good file is silent and exit 0 (the artifact is C, not an executable)
groups.reason: artifact: `build` writes an executable (via C), the self-hosted `build` the generated C
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D4): the self-hosted build's artifact is the generated C, not an executable. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: extensions: --include, --types and -v are the driver's own (the host rejects them)
groups.reason: flags: the driver also has `--include` (an -I alias), `--types` and `-v`
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D3): --include/--types/-v are driver-only flags the host rejects. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: build --lib: the object, its header and the C match the host's shapes
groups.reason: artifact: --lib's object/header/C match the host's shapes now; --no-main does not link
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D4/C9): the object, header and C now match the host's shapes; --no-main does not link without a `main` on this platform (the host's Wasm path), the driver writes the C.

groups.case: build --lib: the object, its header and the C match the host's shapes
groups.reason: artifact: --no-main links an executable without a `main` in the host
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D4/C9): the object, header and C now match the host's shapes; --no-main links an executable in the host, the driver writes the C.

groups.case: build -o: a missing directory fails in both (exit 1, no artifact)
groups.reason: message: a missing `-o` directory is an uncaught `IO.FS.writeFile` exception
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D4/D7): the host lets the C write throw (a machine-dependent trace on stderr); the driver writes one line. Both exit 1 and write nothing.

groups.case: build --header: the driver's header-only mode (the host has no such flag)
groups.reason: artifact: `--header` is the driver's header-only output
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D4): `--header` is a driver-only output mode (the host has no such flag; `--lib` writes OUT.h).

groups.case: warnings: the host warns about a shadowed Prelude (the driver has none yet)
groups.reason: warnings: the host warns (on stdout) about a module root shadowing its own lib
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (A14/D6): the self-hosted loader canonicalises Prelude to the embedded prelude and has no warning channel yet. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: check: a bad file has the same line, severity and kind (the column is the command's start)
groups.reason: column: the host reports the failing term and the declared name
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D6): the self-hosted frontend reports the command's start column. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: -I: an error inside a module (the host nests it under the import)
groups.reason: structure: the host nests a module's errors under its import
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D6/A14): the self-hosted loader reports each error at its own module and position. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: build --llvm: the host has it, the self-hosted backend is C only (C5)
groups.reason: backend: the host builds through textual LLVM IR
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (C5): the self-hosted backend is C only. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: a missing file: both exit 1 (the host's message is an uncaught read)
groups.reason: message: the host lets IO.readFile throw
groups.why: documented self-host parity difference (D6/D7): the driver checks access first and prints one positioned diagnostic. Allow-listed by the user (2026-11-17) for this one case only.

groups.case: known gap: a lambda passed to an unknown callee keeps its body out of the program
groups.reason: known gap: a lambda passed to an unknown callee
groups.why: Joern's LambdaTests fixture. A lambda assigned to a local and invoked in the same method is lowered inline; a lambda passed to a callee whose call site is unknown (`Select`) is still an opaque `fnptr` plus a warning, so its body is absent from the program. The case checks the lowering golden and the skip is the honest report; the golden changes when that gap is fixed.

groups.case: run: program arguments are the driver's (the host's `run` takes flags only)
groups.reason: run: the driver passes the words after FILE to the program
groups.why: The host's `run` takes flags only and rejects trailing arguments (exit 2); the self-hosted driver passes them to the program. That is a documented host caveat, not a regression, and it needs a host-side `run FILE ARG...` before the entry can go.

groups.case: smt: without --trust-smt the refusal is the host's, at the command's start (C15)
groups.reason: column: the host reports the `smt` token, the self-hosted frontend the command's start (D6)
groups.why: The message and exit code agree; only the column differs because the host points at the `smt` token while the driver points at the command's start. Fixing it is D6 positioned diagnostics in the self-hosted frontend.
